entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0387: Vulnerability in crypto-bigint
entry.summary: Multiple timing variability issues in operations intended to be constant-time
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0387

Multiple timing variability issues in operations intended to be constant-time
Reported
October 23, 2026
Issued
October 23, 2026
Package
crypto-bigint (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • crypto-failure
References
  • https://github.com/RustCrypto/crypto-bigint/pull/1365
Patched
  • >=0.7.6

Description

Summary

Several operations intended to be constant-time could execute secret-dependent branches, depending on the compiler and target CPU. These include subtraction, zero counting, division, and Montgomery multiplication.

Additionally, UintRef equality could terminate at the first unequal limb, and BoxedMontyForm::invert branched on whether an inverse exists.

Impact

Applications using affected operations on secret integers may leak information through timing or microarchitectural side channels. This includes information about intermediate arithmetic values, matching limbs, and invertibility.

Such leakage could potentially enable recovery of cryptographic secrets. Practical exploitability depends on the downstream algorithm, compiler, target CPU, and an attacker's ability to observe the side channel.

Resolution

Upgrade to v0.7.6, which removes the identified branches, updates ctutils to include its constant-time fixes, and adds BINSEC-based regression checks using cargo checkct for arithmetic on multiple targets.

Advisory available under CC-BY-4.0 license. Source: https://github.com/RustCrypto/crypto-bigint/pull/1365

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0385: Vulnerability in ctutils
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0385

Non-constant-time mask generation and u128 comparisons
Reported
October 23, 2026
Issued
October 23, 2026
Package
ctutils (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • crypto-failure
References
  • https://github.com/RustCrypto/utils/pull/1569
Related
  • RUSTSEC-2026-0003
Patched
  • >=0.4.4

Description

Summary

The ctutils::Choice type has mask generation functions for each unsigned integer size (u8, u16, u32, u64, u128). These are const fn and therefore can't reuse the asm!-backed mask generation in the cmov crate that's otherwise used to ensure constant-time.

In releases prior to v0.4.4, the generated code from these functions could include a branch on commonly used platforms. This has been corrected in this release and now verified on several platforms using BINSEC.

Additionally, u128 comparison operations provided via ctutils::Choice and intended to work in constant-time were generating branches on 32-bit targets. This has been resolved via a special case implementation of these functions for such targets.

Impact

Branch instructions on secret values can potentially leak such values via covert channels. This can enable attackers to potentially recover such secrets.

Resolution

This has been resolved by calling Choice::to_u8() when generating the mask, which in turn uses black_box as an optimization barrier. Verification that this resulted in the desired change in the generated assembly across a variety of target CPU architectures was performed by BINSEC, which now runs automatically in CI using cargo checkct.

Advisory available under CC-BY-4.0 license. Source: https://github.com/RustCrypto/utils/pull/1569

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0386: Unsoundness in tokio
entry.summary: `AsyncFd::new` and related constructors violate I/O safety
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0386

AsyncFd::new and related constructors violate I/O safety
Reported
October 13, 2026
Issued
October 23, 2026
Package
tokio (crates.io)
Type
INFO Unsound
Categories
  • memory-corruption
Keywords
#io-safety #use-after-free
References
  • https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8587
  • https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/issues/8538
  • https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/issues/8539
Patched
  • >=1.51.6, <1.52.0
  • >=1.53.3
Unaffected
  • <0.3.2
Affected Functions
Version
tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::new
  • >=0.3.2
tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::try_new
  • >=1.37.0
tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::try_with_interest
  • >=1.37.0
tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::with_interest
  • >=0.3.2

Description

tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd provides safe constructors (new, with_interest, try_new, and try_with_interest) that accept any T: AsRawFd rather than requiring proof of ownership or validity of the file descriptor. Because RawFd implements AsRawFd, safe code can construct an AsyncFd from an arbitrary or closed file descriptor, or close/replace the underlying file descriptor while the AsyncFd is still alive.

This violates I/O safety in two ways:

  1. AsyncFd<T> implements AsFd for all T: AsRawFd by calling BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(self.as_raw_fd()), allowing safe code to obtain an arbitrary BorrowedFd<'_> without owning the file descriptor.
  2. Tokio's I/O driver stores a pointer to an internal allocation in the epoll/kqueue user data for registered file descriptors. If the underlying file descriptor is duplicated and then closed while an AsyncFd is alive, and the OS reuses that file descriptor number for a another IO resource on the same runtime, dropping the first AsyncFd deregisters the reused file descriptor number and frees the first while the original file description remains registered in epoll, leading to a use-after-free when a readiness event fires.

Starting in Tokio 1.51.6, 1.53.3, and 1.54.0, AsyncFd::new, AsyncFd::with_interest, AsyncFd::try_new, and AsyncFd::try_with_interest are deprecated in favor of the unsafe constructors AsyncFd::register and AsyncFd::register_with_interest. Callers must ensure that the file descriptor remains valid, open, and unchanged for the lifetime of the AsyncFd.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0384: Vulnerability in tokio
entry.summary: Race condition in `tokio::time::Interval` on Tokio v1.54.0
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0384

Race condition in tokio::time::Interval on Tokio v1.54.0
Reported
October 21, 2026
Issued
October 22, 2026 (last modified: October 24, 2026)
Package
tokio (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-corruption
  • thread-safety
Keywords
#race-condition #use-after-free
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-115567
  • GHSA-5wjr-9356-4wc8
References
  • https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8692
Patched
  • >=1.54.1
Unaffected
  • <1.54.0

Description

Summary

On the multi-threaded runtime, there is a race condition between Interval::poll_tick and the runtime's time driver.

This affects Interval only. Sleep and Timeout are not affected.

Details

In Tokio v1.54.0, a race condition between tokio::time::Interval::poll_tick (including .tick().await) and the runtime time driver can drop an internal timer entry without synchronizing with the driver thread that is firing it. This causes a data race and use-after-free on the timer's waker and task state in safe Rust, leading to assertion panics, task reference-count corruption, or heap memory corruption.

This bug was introduced by https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8458, and it was fixed by https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8692.

Impact

This may lead to crashes and use-after-frees in applications using Interval on a multi-threaded runtime.

Since this issue is known to lead to crashes in production systems, the v1.54.0 release of Tokio has been yanked.

Credits

Thank you to creepycode and carabistouille for reporting this privately using the procedure outlined in our security policy. They both reported the issue independently of each other.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0383: Vulnerability in webpki-root-certs
entry.summary: Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0383

Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates
Reported
October 19, 2026
Issued
October 20, 2026 (last modified: October 21, 2026)
Package
webpki-root-certs (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • crypto-failure
Keywords
#certificate #distrust #x509
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-111943
References
  • https://github.com/rustls/webpki-roots/pull/133
  • https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/
  • https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2083449
Patched
  • >=1.0.10
Unaffected
  • =0.26.11

Description

Affected versions include emSign ECC Root CA - G3, which can allow certificate paths through distrusted emSign intermediates.

Affected versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign intermediate public keys. The private keys corresponding to these intermediates are now well known.

Version 1.0.10+ removes this root.

Version 0.26.11 is a compatibility wrapper that re-exports parent::TLS_SERVER_ROOT_CERTS from its webpki-root-certs 1.x dependency; it contains no separate root certificate list. Its resolved 1.x dependency must be updated to 1.0.10 or later.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.
